newsitem.title: USA: Broin tobacco case opening argument seen July 14.
newsitem.headline: Broin tobacco case opening argument seen July 14.

text.p: The judge in a landmark class-action case against major cigarette makers has told the court he expects opening arguments to begin on July 14, court officials and attorneys on said Tuesday.

Jury selection in the case, known as Norma Broin vs Philip Morris Cos Inc. et. al., began on June 2. By Tuesday, attorneys had selected 113 prospective jurors for a pool that eventually will include up to 125 people.

Attorneys will select a panel of six jurors and 10 alternates from the members of that pool. In selecting the first 113 prospective jurors, they had screened some 400 people. The first five screened Tuesday were excused.
Jury selection was expected to continue Wednesday, Judge Robert Kaye said, with pre-trial hearings on motions and final jury selection set for next week.

In the case, some 60,000 airline flight attendants are seeking $5 billion in damages from nine tobacco defendants, claiming they were sickened by breathing second-hand cigarette smoke on U.S.-based passenger jets.
The closely watched case is the first class action and first second-hand smoke lawsuit against big tobacco to make it to trial. The trial is expected to last up to three months.
Dade County Circuit Judge Robert Kaye also told the court he would hear pre-trial motions on July 8, and expected to begin opening arguments on July 14.

The suit was filed on behalf of thousands of flight attendants across the United States alleging they were sickened by breathing second-hand cigarette smoke on U.S.-based passenger jets. Plaintiffs' attorneys have said they want $5 billion in damages from big tobacco.
It is the first class-action and first second-hand smoke case against the cigarette industry to make it to trial.
